bullets.title: Yields ripping to cycle highs on oil-reflation + Hormuz tensions; Sep Fed hike odds rising
bullets.body: The 10Y Treasury broke above its 4.74% cycle high (touching 4.786% intraday), with Hedgeye and JPM both flagging oil reflation (WTI +2.5-2.8% to ~$88 on Hormuz tanker strikes) as the catalyst. JPM shifted tactically cautious/neutral; Citi notes September Fed hike probability >50% though Citi itself is skeptical given cooler core inflation (core CPI 2.4% YoY). Global bond yields hitting multi-year highs simultaneously — BoJ expected to hike 25bp Sep 18 and again before year-end.

bullets.title: August ISM Manufacturing 54.6, below consensus; new orders -3pts, tariff/Hormuz headwinds cited
bullets.body: August ISM Manufacturing fell 1.0pt to 54.6 vs consensus 55.2, with new orders down 3pts. Prices paid remain historically elevated (15 industries reported higher raw material costs) though flat m/m. ISM respondents cited tariffs, Strait of Hormuz conflict, and AI/electronics supply chain disruptions as key headwinds. Taiwan's manufacturing PMI — which leads U.S. ISM by ~1 month with 70% correlation — also slipped, raising questions about AI/tech momentum leveling.

bullets.title: July JOLTS: openings 7.27M (miss), quits rate fell to 1.9%; Morgan Stanley forecasting August payrolls +65K
bullets.body: July job openings came in at 7.271M vs 7.33M expected, with June revised down 177K to 7.182M. The quits rate fell 10bps to 1.9%, well below the 3% pandemic peak, signaling continued labor market easing. Vacancy rate (openings/unemployed) rose slightly to 1.05 but no longer signals upside risk to unemployment. Morgan Stanley is forecasting a weak August payroll print of just +65K.

bullets.title: VIX at 14-16 range; dealer gamma positive; but September historically +22% VIX, short positioning a setup for spike
bullets.body: VIX rose 3.4% to ~15.43 intraday but remains in Hedgeye's risk range of 14.03-16.28. Positive dealer gamma supports buy-the-dip/fade-strength consolidation rather than a bearish breakdown. However, 22V flags that net short VIX futures positioning at current lows heading into September — a month that historically averages a 22% VIX gain — makes Oct VIX call spreads an attractive asymmetric tail-risk hedge.

bullets.title: Broad market mixed: S&P +0.4% to 7,652 but semis/AI-infrastructure names hit hard in premarket
bullets.body: S&P futures were up ~0.7% to 7,646 while Nasdaq fell ~1.0% as rising yields and oil pressured tech. Semis down 1.4%, memory down 2.2% with MRVL -3.6%, INTC -3.1%, CRWV -3.3%, IREN -3.5% all down >3% in premarket. Energy and defensives poised to outperform on the session. August recap: SPX +2.6%, NDX +4.2%, Mag7 +4.5% driven by TSLA +18.2%, NVDA +9.8%.

bullets.title: Anthropic compute deals set $16M/MW/yr pricing floor, 60% above prior levels — bullish for AI infrastructure
bullets.body: Anthropic signed two 6-year compute deals totaling ~$80B: a $35B deal with Lambda at Hut8's Texas facility and a $45B deal with Nscale in Virginia (460MW), both at ~$16M/MW/year — 60% above the ~$10M/MW/year prior long-term average. Bitdeer's 9MW Asia deal corroborates the same pricing across geographies. Six-year terms signal confidence in GPU longevity; 22V sees this as bullish for CRWV and NBIS revenue visibility.

bullets.title: Fed's Warsh pivots to broader financial conditions lens — implies more tightening work ahead
bullets.body: 22V flags that Fed's Warsh shifted from mechanically following bond-yield signals to a broader financial conditions assessment, concluding that current restraint is limited. The pivot involved visible public cost, making a reversal unlikely. Coupled with JPM's observation that Q3 US GDP is tracking 2.75% annualized and Atlanta Fed Nowcast at 4.6% real (implying >6% nominal), this supports the case for continued monetary tightening pressure.

bullets.title: AI usage services outperforming AI buildout names as cash conversion concern mounts
bullets.body: 22V's High AI Usage Service basket (ex-hyperscalers) carries a 113% cash return ratio and has outperformed +12% over two months as S&P 500 cash return yield sits at an unusually low 56%. Meanwhile AI buildout names face growing cash conversion risk: token/model prices are falling from competition and efficiency gains while hardware and power costs rise. Hedgeye separately flags LLM 'ARR' metrics as non-audited annualized 4-week run-rates — not contractually committed — warranting material valuation discount.

bullets.title: Data center NIMBY pushback peaks before midterms; existing supply (DLR, EQIX) becomes more valuable
bullets.body: Mizuho and Citi/Klein both flag data center political/regulatory backlash as the current headwind — 9 states with pending moratoriums, 20+ with restrictive legislation including a NY state-wide moratorium. Both view this as a near-term overhang through midterms before a year-end rip, with construction constraints making existing DLR and EQIX capacity more valuable as AI demand outpaces new supply. Most active buys on dips: WULF, CRWV, IRM.

bullets.title: Software sector rebound (IGV +47% since April) driven by positioning, not fundamentals — Citi cautions durability
bullets.body: Citi notes the software IGV rally since April is driven by short covering (short interest near 2016/2008 peaks) and narrative rather than broad fundamental improvement; the median software company is still expected to decelerate. A durable re-rating requires tangible AI-driven revenue acceleration. Morgan Stanley separately notes momentum basket has had +/-4% moves 37x YTD, with hedge fund exposure to high-momentum names at only the 19th percentile vs the 12-month window.

bullets.title: Pension funds 112% funded (highest since 2001) — may trigger systematic equity selling in Q3 rebalance
bullets.body: JPM flags pension plans at 112% funding ratios, the highest since 2001, which mechanically triggers equity-to-bond rebalancing flows into quarter-end. This is an additional headwind for equities on top of rising yields and could amplify volatility heading into September end.

bullets.title: Housing demand cracking as mortgage rates hit 6.87%; analyst projects ~0.6% national price decline
bullets.body: Mortgage rates reached ~6.87% (vs 10Y yield at ~4.76%), above the ~6.64% demand-threshold identified by the analyst. Pending sales momentum is weakening, existing home sales are up only ~2.4% YTD but expected to roll over if rates stay elevated, and price cuts have moved above year-ago levels. Geopolitical tensions (Iran/Hormuz) risk pushing rates above 7%. Housing starts and permits sit at multi-year lows, leaving the sector disproportionately exposed to further tightening.

bullets.title: Asia equities: positioning at 40th percentile, near-term cautious but JPM targets MXASJ 1400 on AI capex
bullets.body: JPM notes Asia investor positioning rebounded from 32nd to 40th percentile after Korea leveraged product and Taiwan tech momentum crowding risks largely played out. Near-term caution warranted given restrictive monetary policy, weak cycle indicators, poor seasonality, and no earnings catalysts until October. Medium-term base case remains MXASJ 1400 driven by AI capex adoption and resilience spending; Korea corporate buybacks and EM fund inflows ($19B since July) are emerging positives.

bullets.title: BoJ expected to hike 25bp Sep 18; Japan 2Q profits +24.6% YoY but real economy stalling
bullets.body: Japan 2Q corporate profits surged 24.6% YoY (vs 15.2% consensus) on nominal growth and weak yen, but real consumer spending and real capex both remain below pre-COVID trend. BoJ's policy rate remains well below nominal GDP growth, sustaining an inflationary gap even after two expected hikes by year-end. JGB yields hitting multi-year highs as markets price further tightening, with the Sep 18 +25bp hike seen as near-certain.

bullets.title: JPM global inflation: US headline CPI creeping to 3.5% in Sep, PCE headline at 3.9%; global reflation broadening
bullets.body: JPM's monthly inflation forecast update shows US headline CPI at 3.5% YoY in September (up from 3.4%) and PCE headline at 3.9% (up from 3.8%), with core CPI stable at 2.4%. Euro area CPI accelerating to 3.4%, UK to 3.4%, Japan to 2.3% — a broad global reflation picture consistent with the rising-rates macro backdrop.

bullets.title: Foreign PMIs edge up but momentum set to cool; Korea exports hit record $101B (+68.7% YoY)
bullets.body: PSC's Foreign Manufacturing PMI rose 0.2pt to 51.3% in August but is forecast to cool to 50.4% by July 2027 as DM central banks remain on hiking paths. Korea headline PMI slipped 0.8pt to 52.3% but exports surged to a record $101B (+68.7% YoY, driven by 37.2% YoY export price growth). Taiwan's PMI correlation with U.S. ISM (70%, 1-month lead) warrants monitoring given both slipped m/m.

bullets.title: Hedgeye ETF rotation: adding gold miners (GDX), Turkey (TUR); selling healthcare (XLV), rate-sensitives
bullets.body: Keith McCullough's daily ETF re-rank has GDX and TUR added at position minimums, with AAAU (gold) +100bps and EWP +100bps. Sold XLV, FXH, SLV, HDV and all VCSH/VYM positions. Software (IGV) and healthcare (XLV) are the strongest sector signal styles by rank, while IGV is simultaneously -17 on 1-week rank — reflecting the positioning vs. fundamental tension in software.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex on track to exceed $1T next year; NVDA Rubin CPX GPU revived for 1Q27 with HBM4
bullets.body: MS reports hyperscaler capex expected to exceed $1T next year as AI infrastructure buildout continues. NVDA revived the Rubin CPX GPU for 1Q27 production with HBM4, optimized for inference prefill. NVDA also investing $3.5B in MediaTek via convertibles, with NVLink Fusion adoption. GOOGL's TPU program represents a $200B first-party revenue opportunity per Morgan Stanley's 'Charts That Caught My Eye.'

bullets.title: FTC + 22 states sue Amazon over alleged $20B+ advertiser surcharges via undisclosed reserve pricing
bullets.body: The FTC and 22 state attorneys general sued Amazon alleging it raised advertiser prices through undisclosed reserve-pricing mechanisms on Sponsored Ads, with alleged overcharges exceeding $20B since 2019. Amazon cites improving advertiser ROAS and flat CPCs. Citi views the AMZN weakness as a buyable dip given AWS AI acceleration and retail tailwinds, maintaining Buy at $350 PT.

bullets.title: Brazil macro deteriorating: 2Q private consumption -1.8% q/q saar; JPM cuts 3Q GDP to near-flat
bullets.body: Brazil's 2Q GDP grew 1.9% q/q saar but only due to inventory accumulation; private consumption collapsed 1.8% vs expectations of +2%, with the household saving rate at a historical series high. JPM's 3Q nowcaster points to near-flat growth with its 1.2% q/q saar forecast carrying downside risk. Elevated debt service, rising NPLs, corporate bankruptcies, and labor exhaustion characterize deteriorating private-sector fundamentals, with full-year 2026 GDP ~2% and 2027 at 1.3%.
